**Approved and built on 6 October 2026.** See [the Day 2 review](day2_review.html). The data correction is complete; RDD uses the shared robust interval.


Day 2 asks readers to judge three ways of constructing the missing comparison.
The technical names remain, each attached to a plain question. Participants
predict, read an extract, practise with physical materials, and explain a
provisional judgement. The proposed screens below exclude a title slide.
Timings belong in trainer notes.

These tables record the approved daily review under `HANDOFF.md`. Days 1 and 2 are rebuilt. The historical pre-build notes below are retained; the Day 2 review reports the completed checks and corrected figures.

## Session 1 Reading a difference in changes

**60 minutes.** Keep one four-number comparison and one result row. Ask why
changes would have been similar without GreenWaste. A similar starting level is
not evidence of similar trends. The case has only one before-period; readers
must recognise that the pre-trend assumption cannot be tested here.

| Screen | Participant action and evidence | Minutes |
|---|---|---:|
| 1 A question from yesterday | Recall why before/after alone cannot establish impact | 3 |
| 2 Two groups over time | Predict what subtracting the comparison group's change would add | 4 |
| 3 Complete four numbers | Fill Fiona's four-number sheet; say what each subtraction means | 8 |
| 4 Read the result row | Find the difference-in-differences coefficient, units and interval; one short trainer calculation | 5 |
| 5 What has to be true | Explain parallel trends as similar change without the programme | 6 |
| 6 Would you trust these pictures | Choose between similar trends, already diverging trends and a changing comparison; reveal feedback | 8 |
| 7 What cannot be checked here | Identify the missing earlier observations, and explain why they matter | 5 |
| 8 Mark up a report extract | Work alone, then compare in pairs; state result, assumption and a next question | 10 |
| 9 Repair an AI claim | Remove “the assumption is satisfied” and a threshold conclusion the source does not support | 7 |
| 10 Your evaluator question | Retrieve a concrete question and explain what its answer changes | 4 |

Remove the second long tour through before/after and with/without, repeated
regressions, the full lab visit and long explanations of estimator variants.
Do not restore the reverted AI wall board. The room poll or labelled cards can
capture the prediction; the core practice is on paper.

## Session 2 Reading a jump at a rule

**60 minutes.** Preserve Fiona's eight different jump cards A–H and the A1 wall
number line. Each group handles one card; participants do not receive the full
trainer packet. Reveal the comparison window and the manager-age discontinuity
when each adds evidence to a judgement.

| Screen | Participant action and evidence | Minutes |
|---|---|---:|
| 1 Who is being compared | Recall the city score rule and locate businesses near 58 | 4 |
| 2 Predict the jump | Choose what a cost jump would suggest before opening the result | 4 |
| 3 Read your six businesses | Use one of the eight group cards to estimate a local difference | 10 |
| 4 Place it on the wall | Put card letter and estimated saving on Fiona's number line; explain variation | 6 |
| 5 Read the reported jump | Find the regression-discontinuity result row, interval and local population | 5 |
| 6 How close did they look | Compare two windows; introduce bandwidth as distance from the cut-off | 5 |
| 7 Did something else jump | Predict, then reveal manager age; explain why this challenges the causal reading | 7 |
| 8 Complete a short credibility check | Judge the rule, nearby comparison, other discontinuities and reach | 9 |
| 9 Check an AI recommendation | Correct the claim that a local estimate supports the whole city | 6 |
| 10 Your next question | Write one evidence-seeking question, independently | 4 |

Keep one brief trainer demonstration, after a prediction. Drop repeated slope
interpretations, extensive placebo runs, long sample-window sliders and a
second AI exercise. Use the same computed model and interval on screen and
paper. The existing handoff flags an ordinary-versus-robust interval discrepancy;
resolve it explicitly in the shared calculation before building.

### Data correction to decide before this session is built

Eight city records printed with score 58 have non-participation because the
generator assigns participation before rounding. The handoff requires approval
before changing the CSV. A clean score-rule case would assign participation
from the rounded score and regenerate those records' outcomes consistently,
then refresh affected Day 1 and Day 2 figures and packs. The current Day 1
rebuild leaves the CSV unchanged. Until corrected, do not describe observed
compliance with the displayed score as perfect.

## Session 3 Reading a matched comparison

**75 minutes, including a five-minute break.** Preserve Fiona's seven profile
cards per group and optional walking version. Let participants match on
pre-programme characteristics before showing outcomes. Keep nearest-neighbour
matching as the actual method; do not call it propensity-score matching.

| Screen | Participant action and evidence | Minutes |
|---|---|---:|
| 1 Which comparison would be fair | Predict why an unmatched cost gap could mislead | 4 |
| 2 Read the profiles | Find pre-programme characteristics that could affect costs | 5 |
| 3 Find the twins | Groups use Fiona's seven profile cards; optional walking version | 12 |
| 4 Open their costs | Reveal outcomes only after matching; calculate or read the difference | 5 |
| 5 Read the matched result | Name who is compared, find the estimate and identify unmatched records | 6 |
| 6 What was used to match | Explain the actual nearest-neighbour method in plain language; one trainer demo | 5 |
| 7 Break | Protect the break | 5 |
| 8 Leave out manager age | Predict, then reveal the changed estimate; connect the difference to selection | 6 |
| 9 What remains unmeasured | Distinguish balanced observed characteristics from an unmeasured cause | 5 |
| 10 Mark up the report extract | Individual reading, then pair feedback, using comparison and limitation | 8 |
| 11 Write a provisional judgement | Support each conclusion with the source; name a useful next question | 6 |
| 12 Repair an AI assurance | Remove claims that every business was matched and that matching removes all bias | 5 |
| 13 Your question from memory | Independent close with the purpose of the question | 3 |

Remove the traffic-camera comparison, extra matching variants, the second full
case and repeated model runs. “Similar on recorded characteristics” must not
become “identical” or “randomly assigned”. A matched comparison can be credible,
but its causal interpretation still relies on the absence of important
unmeasured differences and an adequate comparison pool.

## Materials and review checks

Use one two-sided participant sheet per session, with the shared reading layout
from Day 1. Keep group cards and printing instructions in the trainer packet.
Preserve the existing A1 activities and their distribution logic. Keep AI source
checking in every session without requiring an AI account. Assess each reader's
independent final question and reason; room vote movement alone is not a score.

For each deck, check every screen, run the single trainer cell, open every
evidence reveal and test keyboard controls. Render all changed print pages and
compare their calculated figures with the deck. Publish unlinked previews after
those checks. The shortened Day 2 route is pending review.
